questions.question: Custom-ALPN UCAN check fires BEFORE iroh-blobs handoff (matches Spike A2 + Spike H+1.2 Experiment 2)?
questions.answer: YES. The handler's 6-arm pipeline at ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:418-533 runs (1) unresolved-peer short-circuit → (2) audience-binding == EndpointId → (3) UCAN nbf <= now < exp → (4) revocation check → (5) AuthorizationGrant::verify_binding (covers A-1/A-2/A-3) → (6) RestrictedScope.roots allowlist; ONLY on all-pass returns Ok(()) and only then does the caller hand the iroh Connection to iroh_blobs::provider::handle_connection. Test seam serve_request_for_test increments the dispatch counter ONLY after positive validation; pin tf3e_dispatch_to_iroh_blobs_only_after_positive_validation verifies counter unchanged on reject + +1 on accept. The actual iroh_blobs::provider::handle_connection call is honestly NAMED-as-out-of-scope at the swap-point (production wire-up at G-CORE-3-real-iroh-blobs integration wave); the validation-arm proof is end-to-end against the test seam, which is the correct wave-3e scope.

questions.question: Two-CID mapping (plaintext_cid → ciphertext_cid) persists to redb in production; the spike's in-memory version isn't shipping?
questions.answer: YES (structurally correct, with honest scope-marker). The persistent plaintext_cid → ciphertext_cid mapping lives in benten-graph's redb backend at TWO_CID_MAP_TABLE (redb_backend.rs:111-112) keyed via TwoCidMap::partition_table_key(did, plaintext_cid) — durability pin tf3d_two_cid_mapping_durable_across_reopen at tf3d_two_cid_mapping_roundtrip.rs:208 asserts cross-reopen recovery + tf3d_mapping_table_tamper_yields_typed_integrity_error covers tamper. The benten-sync TwoCidStore (two_cid_store.rs) is the wave-3e adapter that holds (i) a local mapping cache + (ii) the ciphertext-bytes store; its module docstring (lines 28-42) honestly names the production swap-points: the mapping moves to the redb backend, and the ciphertext_bytes Mutex<BTreeMap<...>> swaps for iroh_blobs::FsStore. This is the correct decomposition (durable substrate already lives in benten-graph; the wave-3e adapter exists ONLY so the ALPN handler can land its per-request UCAN + scope arms without dragging iroh-blobs as a workspace dep mid-wave). The spike-only in-memory store IS NOT what production reads — production reads the redb TwoCidMap directly through benten-graph::RedbBackend.

questions.question: Per-chunk-AEAD: chunk_size = IROH_BLOCK_SIZE (16 KiB); threshold ≥64 KiB; range-fetch slice is independently decryptable?
questions.answer: YES. The IROH_BLOCK_SIZE constant is re-exported from benten_crypto_suite::aead::IROH_BLOCK_SIZE = 16 * 1024 (aead.rs:52) into benten-graph as aead_wrap::IROH_BLOCK_SIZE (aead_wrap.rs:56). WHOLE_AEAD_THRESHOLD = 64 KiB re-exported (aead_wrap.rs:63 / aead.rs:56). EncryptedNode::encrypt dispatches on plaintext.len() < WHOLE_AEAD_THRESHOLD (aead_wrap.rs:118-131). ChunkedCiphertext::encrypt slices plaintext.chunks(IROH_BLOCK_SIZE) sealing each independently under aad_per_chunk(plaintext_cid, chunk_index) (aead_wrap.rs:229-235). Independent decryptability proven by free-function decrypt_chunk (aead_wrap.rs:327-338) which takes a single chunk + index + plaintext_cid + key. Pinned: tf3d_iroh_block_size_is_16_kib_exactly + tf3d_whole_aead_threshold_is_64_kib + tf3d_large_node_chunked_to_16_kib_each_independent_decrypt + the in-module unit test iroh_block_size_constant_is_16_kib at aead_wrap.rs:663. V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md §15.g aligns. The 16-KiB constant is wire-format-load-bearing + bytewise-pinned per item 4.

questions.question: AAD-binds-plaintext-CID rebinding-attack defense actually fires (cross-check w/ L2 adversarial)?
questions.answer: YES — comprehensively. (a) Whole-arm: aad_whole_content(plaintext_cid) at aead.rs:210-215 prepends 'benten-aead:whole:' || plaintext_cid; pinned by tf3d_aad_binds_plaintext_cid_rebinding_attack_defeated which mounts a valid ciphertext under a different plaintext-CID via with_aad_plaintext_cid_for_test seam at aead_wrap.rs:155-166 and asserts AeadError::Authentication. (b) Chunked-arm: aad_per_chunk(plaintext_cid, chunk_index) at aead.rs:221-227 also binds the chunk_index as a u64-LE; pinned by tf3d_cross_chunk_rebinding_fails_aad_binds_chunk_index (presents chunk-N's bytes at index-M and asserts auth-fail). (c) Stable in-module tests rebinding_attack_fails + cross_chunk_rebinding_fails at aead_wrap.rs:617 + 642 cover the same surface as smoke. The defense is structural: the suite_unwrap call at aead_wrap.rs:277 + 293 reconstructs AAD from the envelope's plaintext_cid field — any post-seal AAD-mutation breaks Poly1305 verification at the cipher-suite layer. No silent-fallback path identified.

questions.question: Drop bundle envelope-sig validation; per-Node AEAD authentication; defense-in-depth pin honest (pim-18; sig-layer NF-4 strip-resistance separately exercised post-fix-up)?
questions.answer: YES — with one OBS noted under findings. Layer-1 envelope-sig binds the bundle header MINUS content (envelope_sig.rs:80-102: build_envelope_message clones bundle, zeroes envelope_sig + issuer_verifying_key + content, encodes header, prepends domain-tag 'benten/g-core-3f/drop-bundle-envelope/v1'); this is the documented defense-in-depth design — a content-byte tamper does NOT break envelope-sig (caught at Layer-3 AEAD-tag). Layer-2 grant binding-sig (verify_binding at authorization_grant.rs:591) covers A-1/A-2/A-3 uniformly per RATIFIED-S&C §R3. Layer-3 per-Node AEAD: each EncryptedContent decodes via decode_encrypted_node + decrypts via benten_graph::aead_wrap::decrypt; AEAD-tag failure surfaces typed PerNodeAeadAuthenticationFailed (bundle.rs:147-153 + bundle.rs:417-422). consume_offline runs the three layers in order with fail-fast at envelope-sig BEFORE any decrypt attempt (proven by consume_offline_with_dec_counter_for_test + tf3f_tampered_envelope_sig_fails_before_per_node_decrypt). The per-Node-attestation field is HONESTLY disclosed as a SIZED PLACEHOLDER (bundle.rs:265-274 + 728-749 + the test pin tf3f_per_node_attestation_size_overhead_under_12_percent at lines 125-167 explicitly states this); PerNodeSignatureInvalid variant is documented as 'reserved-but-unconstructed until G-CORE-9 v1-interface freeze upgrades per_node_attestation to typed Vec<Signature>'. This matches pim-18 SHAPE-not-SUBSTANCE discipline: the substance (real per-Node Ed25519 sigs) is correctly named-as-future + the size-reservation pin keeps the future field honest. The defense-in-depth at G-CORE-3f is genuinely 2 cryptographic layers (envelope-sig + per-Node-AEAD-tag); the docstring states this explicitly. NF-4 strip-resistance (committing-combiner) is the crypto-suite layer's concern not the Drop bundle's; not in this lens's scope.

findings.title: Public `_for_test` helpers + connection-less validate_request lack #[doc(hidden)] discipline; production misuse risk for validate_request (silently bypasses Arm-2 audience binding).
findings.evidence: Four functions are `pub` but are intended for test seams or non-production callers: (a) `validate_request` (no-conn-context arm) substitutes the grant's OWN audience_pubkey as the connection EndpointId at line 393-405 — this STRUCTURALLY bypasses Arm 2 (audience-binding check) for any production caller that mistakenly uses it instead of `validate_request_for_connection`. The docstring at 366-378 warns 'Production callers should use validate_request_for_connection (audience-binding is the §R3 contract; skipping it is a confidentiality hazard)' but the function remains pub + lacks #[doc(hidden)]. The sealed-discipline (CLAUDE.md #19 / sealed CapabilityPolicy precedent in §3-meta) would prefer pub(crate) or #[doc(hidden)]. (b) record_revocation_for_test (named _for_test) is pub without #[doc(hidden)] — drift-detect scanner sees it as a public production surface. (c) serve_request_for_test similar. (d) endpoint_id_from_public_key_no_parsing is pub without #[doc(hidden)] AND without _for_test suffix — it IS a production helper but doc-block at 567-575 says 'Production wire-up reaches the iroh API directly through verifying_key_to_endpoint_id / endpoint_id_to_verifying_key' which suggests it's the test-time convenience. Cross-reference: dispatch_count_for_test (line 357) and EndpointIdBytes::to_bytes_for_test (line 594) ARE correctly marked #[doc(hidden)]; the discipline is recognized but applied inconsistently.
findings.impact: validate_request silently bypassing audience-binding is the load-bearing concern: a production caller (e.g. a future engine-side wire-up author) that grabs the simpler-looking 'validate this request' API skips the A-2 audience-substitution defense entirely. The docstring warning is necessary but insufficient — type-system / visibility enforcement is the standard discipline (sealed-trait precedent; pub vs pub(crate)).
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW (clause-a inline orchestrator-direct in the R6-R1-FP wave): add `#[doc(hidden)]` to the 4 functions named above + consider tightening `validate_request` visibility to `pub(crate)` (or renaming to `validate_request_unbound_for_test` with #[doc(hidden)]) so production callers cannot accidentally skip Arm 2. The fix is ~10 LOC + carries no behaviour change for the wave-3e test surface.

findings.title: std::sync::Mutex contention point on revocation lookups + bytes-fetch under concurrent inbound ALPN connections; production-scale concern named but not yet measured.
findings.evidence: The wave-3e handler structure assumes concurrent inbound iroh connections share a single UcanBlobsHandler (revocation Mutex locked on every per-request validation at line 477-485) + a single TwoCidStore (mapping Mutex locked on every plaintext→ciphertext resolve at line 102-108; bytes Mutex locked on every ciphertext_bytes fetch at line 116-122). Under wave-3e in-memory + ~zero-concurrency tests this is fine. At production scale with real iroh-blobs + concurrent peers + a real revocation backend, every request serializes through these mutexes. The TwoCidStore docstring (line 60-62) explicitly mentions 'Thread-safe (interior Mutex) so the wave-3e ALPN handler can be shared across concurrent inbound connections without an outer Arc<RwLock<_>> ceremony' — acknowledging the structure but not the contention asymptote.
findings.impact: Wave-3e correctness: PASS. Production-scale throughput is a known carry that will surface when iroh-blobs lands at integration wave + a concurrency benchmark is wired. Not a freeze-blocker (the swap-point IS the named-destination); naming it now so it doesn't surface as a surprise at G-CORE-9 close.
findings.disposition: OBS / BELONGS-NAMED-NOW into docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md or the G-CORE-3-real-iroh-blobs integration wave's pre-work brief; HARD RULE 12 clause-b destination required. Recommend orchestrator add a one-line carry row at the integration wave's brief: 'measure revocation-Mutex + TwoCidStore-Mutex contention under N concurrent connections; consider RwLock if read-heavy / sharded-by-DID if write-contention surfaces; the named swap from in-memory to backend is the natural window.'
